title: Tonya Z NDE 160
content:
I was hit by a car on a pedestrian crossing. I came to the realization of what was happening once I saw my own body. I saw it from the viewpoint of the corner of the room, away from the accident site. I was unconscious at the time. For the first few seconds of the NDE, I felt that I was accepted there. Warmth, immense love, and an incredible feeling of wisdom surrounded me. It felt like I had arrived home from somewhere. I felt that I was given an opportunity to stay in that space. However, as soon as I realized what had happened, I panicked and allowed fear to pervade my whole soul. Amazingly with no body, I still had a voice. I shouted with such powerful force and in such terror ‘this is a mistake!’ (that, I remember vividly). It was at this point that I felt there was a distinctive repulsion of these fearful feelings within the contrasting wisdom that surrounded me. (Throughout this seemingly short experience, I feel that I had my back to something and was looking the whole time down at my body.) I was not in harmony with the surroundings; perhaps I was immature. I felt that I was sent away. I feel that I did not choose to come back. I regained consciousness as I was being carried out towards the ambulance. My feeling is that it was possible that my heart had stopped and that possibly the fright of seeing my own body may have started it again. I cannot verify this idea, as this was never monitored. The experience was both one of a moment of true warmth, wisdom and happiness and, at the same time, one of emotional trauma for me

stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Experience emphasized an out-of-body view of her body from a room corner and an immediate sense of acceptance/warmth/wisdom, followed by panic and an abrupt feeling of being 'sent away' and regaining consciousness while being carried to the ambulance; no tunnel, beings, boundary, or life review described.
stage_sequence.simultaneous_stage_detail: She reported feeling she was 'looking the whole time down at my body' while also experiencing the surrounding warmth/wisdom and later fear.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: She described a 'distinctive repulsion' of her fearful feelings within the surrounding wisdom, and that she had her 'back to something' while looking down at her body.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “this is a mistake!”; “It felt like I had arrived home from somewhere.”
